newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech c.bank says recent crown rates "positive".
newsitem.headline: Czech c.bank says recent crown rates "positive".

text.p: Developments in the Czech crown's exchange rate in recent days have been positive, a senior central banker said on Friday.

"We see the development of the crown over the past few days as positive. The rate has been steady around 18.5 to the Deutsche mark and stable. We view this as positive," bank board member Ludek Niedermayer told a news conference.
The crown stood at 18.529 to the mark at 1110 GMT, barely changed from the opening and Thursday levels.
It edged up slightly on Thursday morning after better-than-expected figures for first-quarter GDP growth.
The central bank floated the crown on May 27 after a wave of speculative short-selling. The currency had previously been fixed within a band of plus/minus 7.5 percent against a dollar/mark basket.
"When we removed the band, people said the crown would weaken sharply but this did not necessarily have to be the case," Niedermayer said.
The crown is currently trading around 6.34 percent below the old basket's parity.
The crown came under pressure because of investor anxiety at widening trade and current account deficits. The market is now focusing on May foreign trade figures due to be released on Monday.
